title: Cartesian squares in fine saturated log schemes
statement: Let $A,B,C,D$ be locally Noetherian fine saturated log schemes, with log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and let $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to D$, $c:A\to C$, and $d:C\to D$. The square commutes when $b\circ a=d\circ c$ as log morphisms, including their maps on all relative etale log sections. It is cartesian in the category of fs log schemes if it commutes and, for every locally Noetherian fs log scheme $Z$ and log morphisms $p:Z\to B$, $q:Z\to C$ with $b\circ p=d\circ q$, there exists a unique log morphism $r:Z\to A$ with $a\circ r=p$ and $c\circ r=q$. These equalities are equalities of full log morphisms. No condition that the underlying square of schemes be cartesian is included.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.9--3.3.11, printed p.108: saturated log base change; VI 2.2, printed p.72: the fs Galois diagonal.
